subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: What should OpenClaw do by default when an agent turn emits tool-call-shaped assistant text instead of structured toolCall/toolUse content?
rationale: The current code intentionally mixes warning-only diagnostics, bounded compatibility promotion, and scoped Gateway HTTP enforcement; choosing stricter rejection, forced retry, or promotion changes both the security boundary and local-model compatibility contract.

options.title: Define bounded enforcement
options.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

options.title: Keep compatibility default
options.body: Document fake tool-call-looking text as provider/model incompatibility and accept warning-only behavior unless a narrower provider path opts into promotion or required tool_choice.

options.title: Split broader claim checks
options.body: Limit this issue to syntactic fake tool-call text and keep natural-language success-claim verification under the broader response-gate or claim-ledger items.

recommendation.title: Define bounded enforcement
recommendation.body: Choose the exact warning, suppression, promotion, retry, or fail-closed contract and implement it with focused agent-loop, provider, Gateway, and docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a core agent-runtime security/default policy decision, and this handle has the strongest current history signal around the promotion boundary plus prior maintainer-facing review context.
